instructions.manual_exchange_notice: Upload this CHATGPT_PACKAGE.json independently in a fresh chat. VideoHoarder never uploads data automatically.

quality_rubric.grounding: Every material transcript-derived conclusion cites canonical segment_ids.
quality_rubric.coverage: Process every exact VIDEO_ID and every requested feature.
quality_rubric.semantic_synthesis: Write semantic summaries that consolidate meaning, argument, method and implications; do not concatenate or lightly rewrite transcript lines.
quality_rubric.timeline: Create boundaries only when the substantive topic changes; merge adjacent fragments about the same point.
quality_rubric.claims: Extract all consequential factual, medical, safety, financial, legal, causal, quantitative and recommendation claims; grade risk and external-verification need.
quality_rubric.entities: Perform named-entity recognition, merge aliases, type entities using the controlled list, and omit generic nouns.
quality_rubric.taxonomy: Use only controlled categories and canonical non-promotional tags.
quality_rubric.editorial: Make assessments specific to this video's evidence, value, limitations and audience; never reuse boilerplate.
quality_rubric.consistency: Use the same canonical evidence across summaries, timeline, claims, intake and editorial assessment.
quality_rubric.specificity: Preserve useful names, quantities, steps and qualifications; avoid generic filler.
quality_rubric.uncertainty: Distinguish source claims, supplied support, interpretation and external-verification needs.
quality_rubric.comments: Cluster only structured supplied comment records and report total, included count and sampling limitations; popularity is not factual verification.
quality_rubric.clips: Select only self-contained clips lasting 30-180 seconds, with valid non-overlapping timestamps and a video-specific purpose.

instructions.instructions: Use only the evidence embedded in this independently processed package and obey response_schema.feature_contracts, controlled_taxonomy, and formal_json_schema. Process every exact VIDEO_ID and return one final JSON object with no prose or markdown. All features must use the same canonical sentence-level transcript segments. Do not claim that you watched or listened to a video. Produce semantic synthesis rather than extractive transcript rewrites. Build timelines from meaningful topic boundaries. Perform complete risk-aware claim extraction and proper named-entity recognition. Make editorial_assessment.v1 a video-specific ChatGPT's Take, not boilerplate. Separate: (1) what the source says, (2) what the supplied evidence supports, (3) your interpretation, and (4) what remains uncertain or requires external verification. Cite canonical transcript segment_ids for transcript-derived conclusions. Downgrade confidence for partial/low evidence. If canonical segments are absent, do not produce transcript-derived summaries, timelines, claims, transcript-derived entities, or clips; metadata/comment-derived fields must identify their source and unsupported fields must be empty/unknown with the limitation. Validate structure, semantics, provenance, duplicates, timestamps, word counts and cross-feature consistency before returning PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNINGS or FAIL.

editorial_assessment.v1.chatgpt_take: A concise, evidence-grounded interpretation—not a repetition of the summary.

practical_value.explanation: Why the material is or is not useful.

credibility_assessment.explanation: Assess presentation and supplied support without pretending to externally fact-check.

editorial_assessment.v1.interpretation_limits: What cannot be concluded from the supplied evidence.

🎁 FREE RESOURCE
I've put all 10 tools, every GitHub link, and the exact prompts I used inside our free "Staying Ahead" community. 
👉 https://links.stayingahead.com/YT63

These 10 free and open-source AI tools do the same job as the paid ones you're already paying for — image, voice, video, coding, even automation agents. All 100% free, all running on your own computer, and you don't need to know a single line of code. If you can copy and paste, you can run every one of them.

I use AI for basically everything, so I've paid for almost every tool out there. WOOD CAR CARVING — FULL PROCESS MASTER PROMPT

A cinematic ASMR woodcarving montage, filmed in continuous real workshop time — not sped up, not rushed. The pacing should feel like a slow satisfying time-lapse: fast enough to show progress, slow enough that every cut and motion is clearly visible and believable. Same hands, same workbench, same lighting throughout for full continuity — this must feel like one uninterrupted crafting session, not disconnected clips.

A rough, unshaped chunk of hardwood — bark still visible on one edge, natural grain, irregular surface — is placed onto a worn wooden workbench. A pencil is used to sketch the rough side-profile silhouette of the [Vehicle] directly onto the wood block as a carving guide. Overhead workshop lighting, warm and directional, casting soft shadows across the grain.

Hands use a large carving knife and mallet-driven chisel to remove the bulk excess wood, following the sketched guideline. Large chunks and thick curls of wood fall away and land on the workbench, where they remain and begin to accumulate into a small pile — they do not disappear between cuts. The block slowly reveals the rough silhouette of a car body. Visible tool marks remain on the surface at this stage — intentionally rough, not yet refined.

Switching to a smaller detail chisel, hands carve the hood line, windshield angle, roofline, and rear slope with clean deliberate strokes. Wood shavings continue building up around the base of the model on the workbench. The car's proportions become clearly recognizable by the end of this shot.

Using a narrow gouge chisel, hands carve out the wheel arch curves on both visible sides. A fine scoring blade is used to etch clean door seam lines, a trunk line, and panel gaps into the surface — subtle but visible detail lines that read as doors and panels rather than a solid block.

Hands wrap sandpaper around a fingertip and sand the entire body in smooth back-and-forth motions, progressively smoothing the chisel marks. Fine wood dust drifts and settles onto the bench and the shavings pile below. The wood grain becomes visibly smoother and catches the light differently than the rough stage.
SHOT 6 — Fine Detail with Rotary Tool:

A rotary Dremel-style tool is used at close macro range to carve the front grille slats, headlight recesses, and side mirror mounts. Fine wood dust sprays lightly with each pass. This is the most intricate, slowest-paced shot — real-time, not time-lapsed, to let the detail register.

Separately hand-carved small wooden wheels — already rounded and smoothed in an earlier stage, shown briefly in-hand — are fitted onto axle pegs and pressed into the wheel wells until they sit flush. Tiny carved details — a spoiler piece, side mirrors — are dabbed with wood glue and pressed into place by hand, held for a beat to set.

Hands use a soft brush to sweep all the accumulated wood shavings and dust off the workbench and off the model itself, revealing the clean, fully carved and assembled wooden car sitting alone on the now-clear bench. This is the calm-before-the-finish beat.

An airbrush sprays a smooth, even, glossy paint finish onto the body in slow controlled passes, the matte raw wood transforming into a rich, reflective, showroom-glossy surface. Chrome-finish rims are pressed onto the wheels as the final touch.
Match-cut from the finished glossy miniature to the real, full-sized [Vehicle] parked on a wet reflective city street at night.

STYLE: 8K resolution, hyper-detailed wood grain texture in every carving shot, macro studio lighting with warm directional shadows during the crafting shots, shifting to moody anamorphic urban bokeh only in the final transition shot. Ultra-photorealistic. Continuous realistic hand movement — natural grip, natural tool contact, no floating or disconnected motion. Wood shavings and dust persist and accumulate realistically across shots rather than resetting.
SOUND DESIGN (ASMR): chisel taps, wood scraping and splintering, sandpaper friction, rotary tool whirring, soft brush sweeping, airbrush hiss. No music, no voiceover.
